versions.title_at_revision: Throttle and antidetonant injection system controls.
versions.text:
(a) There must be a separate throttle control for each engine.
(b) Throttle controls must be arranged to allow ready synchronization of all engines by--
  (1) Separate control of each engine; and
  (2) Simultaneous control of all engines.
(c) Each throttle control must provide a positive and immediately responsive means of controlling its engine.
(d) Each antidetonant injection system control must be in the throttle controls. However, the antidetonant injection pump may have a separate control.

(a) There must be a separate throttle control for each engine.
(b) Throttle controls must be arranged to allow ready synchronization of all engines by--
  (1) Separate control of each engine; and
  (2) Simultaneous control of all engines.
(c) Each throttle control must provide a positive and immediately responsive means of controlling its engine.
[(d) Each fluid injection other than fuel system control must be in the throttle controls. However, the injection system pump may have a separate control.
(e) If a power or thrust control incorporates a fuel shutoff feature, the control must have a means to prevent the inadvertent movement of the control into the shutoff position. The means must--
  (1) Have a positive lock or stop a the idle position; and
  (2) Require a separate and distinct operation to place the control in the shutoff position.]
